claims.text: Intermediate-layer high-entropy alloys for plasma-facing components are typically based on refractory elements such as Cr, Mo, Nb, Ta, and W.
Adding 5–10 at.% Cu to the HEA will improve its heat-transfer capability.
Adding 5–10 at.% Cu will not significantly compromise structural integrity under plasma-facing reactor conditions.
The proposed performance will persist at temperatures up to 1000°C under thermal cycling and mechanical loading representative of plasma-facing reactor environments.
Cu added at 5–10 at.% will form a solid solution with Cu atoms dispersed in the HEA matrix.
The Cu-modified HEA will retain a single-phase structure.
Cu has high intrinsic thermal conductivity.
Cu addition increases the alloy's electronic thermal conductivity because of Cu's high intrinsic conductivity.
Solid-solution strengthening from the HEA matrix will preserve mechanical integrity after Cu addition.
The Cu-modified alloy will have at least 20% higher thermal conductivity than the Cu-free baseline HEA.
The Cu-modified alloy's yield strength will remain within 10% of the baseline value under reactor-relevant conditions.
The Cu-modified alloy's ductility will remain within 10% of the baseline value under reactor-relevant conditions.
Current Cu-free intermediate-layer HEAs have moderate thermal conductivity.
Current Cu-free intermediate-layer HEAs have high structural integrity.
Cu content above its solubility limit in the HEA matrix may cause phase segregation.
Cu-induced phase segregation may reduce the alloy's mechanical properties.
The Cu solubility limit is not established for the specific HEA system proposed.
Long-term irradiation may affect the phase stability of the Cu-modified HEA.
